paragraphs: Brown-Forman Corporation (the "Company," "Brown-Forman," "we," "us," or "our" below) was incorporated under the laws of the State of Delaware in 1933, successor to a business founded in 1870 as a partnership and later incorporated under the laws of the Commonwealth of Kentucky in 1901. We primarily manufacture, distill, bottle, import, export, market, and sell a wide variety of beverage alcohol products under recognized brands. We employ approximately 4,900 people (excluding individuals who work on a part-time or temporary basis) on six continents, including approximately 1,900 people in the United States (approximately 7% of whom are represented by a union) and 700 people in Louisville, Kentucky, USA, home of our world headquarters. According to International Wine & Spirit Research (IWSR), we are the largest American-owned premium-plus spirits company. We are a "controlled company" under New York Stock Exchange rules because the Brown family owns more than 50% of our voting stock.
For a discussion of recent developments, see "Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations – Executive Summary."

Beginning in 1870 with Old Forester Kentucky Straight Bourbon Whisky – our founding brand – and spanning the generations since, we have built a portfolio of more than 40 spirit and ready-to-drink (RTD) cocktail brands that includes some of the best-known and most loved trademarks in our industry. The most important and iconic brand in our portfolio is Jack Daniel's Tennessee Whiskey, the #1 selling American whiskey in the world.1 Within the Jack Daniel's portfolio, Jack Daniel's 14-Year-Old Tennessee Whiskey took home honors for World's Best Tennessee Whiskey and Jack Daniel's Bonded won the award for Best Tennessee Whiskey (No Age Statement) at the 2026 World Whiskies Awards. Our premium bourbon, Old Forester, was recognized by the San Francisco Spirits Competition in 2026, where both Old Forester 1870 Original Batch and Old Forester 1897 Bottled in Bond won Double Gold (the highest honor).

headings: Risks Related to Our Business and Operations
Our business performance depends substantially on the continued health of the Jack Daniel's family of brands.

Changes to our route-to-consumer models and consolidation among beverage alcohol producers, distributors, wholesalers, suppliers, and retailers could hinder the marketing, sale, or distribution of our products.
We are subject to risks from changes to the trade policies, tariffs, and import and export regulations of the United States and foreign governments.
Production facility disruption could adversely affect our business.
The inherent uncertainty in supply/demand forecasting could adversely affect our business, particularly with respect to our aged products.
Higher costs or unavailability of water, raw materials, product ingredients, or labor could adversely affect our financial results.
Unfavorable economic conditions could negatively affect our operations and results.
We might not succeed in our strategies for investments, acquisitions, dispositions, and other strategic transactions.
Negative publicity or our inability or failure to recognize, respond to, and effectively manage the increased impact of social media could affect our business performance.
Product recalls or other product liability claims could materially and adversely affect our sales.
Our failure to attract or retain key talent could adversely affect our business.
Our business faces various risks related to health epidemics and pandemics that could materially and adversely affect our business, our operations, our cash flows, and our financial results.
Risks Related to Our Global Operations
Our global business is subject to commercial, political, and financial risks.
A failure to comply with anti-corruption laws, trade sanctions and restrictions, or similar laws or regulations may have a material adverse effect on our business and financial results.
Fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates relative to the U.S. dollar could have a material adverse effect on our financial results.
A downgrade or potential downgrade of our credit ratings could adversely impact our borrowing costs and access to credit and capital markets, which could negatively affect our financial condition.
Legal and Regulatory Risks
National and local governments may adopt regulations or undertake investigations that could limit our business activities or increase our costs.
Tax increases and changes in tax rules could adversely affect our financial results.
Our ability to market and sell our products depends heavily on societal attitudes toward drinking and governmental policies that both flow from and affect those attitudes.
Significant additional labeling, warning requirements, or limitations on the availability of our products could inhibit sales of affected products.
Counterfeiting or inadequate protection of our intellectual property rights could adversely affect our business prospects.
Litigation and legal disputes could expose our business to financial and reputational risk.
Risks Related to Cybersecurity and Data Privacy
Risks Related to Our Ownership and Corporate Governance Structure
The Brown family has the ability to control the outcome of matters submitted for stockholder approval.
paragraphs: We believe the following discussion identifies the material risks and uncertainties that could adversely affect our business. If any of the following risks were actually to occur, our business, results of operations, cash flows, or financial condition could be materially and adversely affected. Additional risks not currently known to us, or that we currently deem to be immaterial, could also materially and adversely affect our business, results of operations, cash flows, or financial condition.

The Jack Daniel's family of brands is the primary driver of our revenue, and Jack Daniel's is an iconic global trademark with a loyal consumer fan base. We invest much effort and many resources to protect and preserve the brand's reputation for authenticity, craftsmanship, and quality. A brand's reputational value is based in large part on consumer perceptions, and even an isolated incident that causes harm – particularly one resulting in widespread negative publicity – could adversely influence these perceptions and erode consumer trust and confidence in the brand. Significant damage to the brand equity of the Jack Daniel's family of brands would adversely affect our business. Given the importance of Jack Daniel's to our overall success, a significant or sustained decline in sales of our Jack Daniel's products, as a result of negative publicity or otherwise, would have a negative effect on our financial results. Additionally, if we are not successful in our efforts to maintain or increase the relevance of the Jack Daniel's brand to current and future consumers, our business and operating results could suffer.

We use various business models to market and distribute our products in different countries around the world. In the United States, we sell our products either to distributors for resale to retail outlets or e-commerce retailers or, in those states that control alcohol sales, to state governments who then sell them to retail customers and consumers. In our non-U.S. markets, we use a variety of route-to-consumer models, and, in many markets, we rely on third parties to distribute, market, and sell our products. We own and operate 17 distribution companies in 18 countries. Transitioning from a third-party distribution model to an owned-distribution model involves a significant undertaking, and subjects us to additional operational and execution risks associated with each affected geographic region. If we are unsuccessful in our route-to-consumer strategies, including any transition to owned distribution, the sale and marketing of our products could be disrupted.

Changes to any of our route-to-consumer models or distributors in important markets could result in temporary or longer-term sales disruption, higher costs, and harm to other business relationships we might have with that distributor. Disruption of our distribution network or fluctuations in our product inventory levels at distributors, wholesalers, or retailers could negatively affect our results for a particular period. Moreover, other suppliers, as well as wholesalers and retailers of our brands, offer products that compete directly with ours for shelf space, promotional displays, and consumer purchases.

Pricing (including price promotions, discounting, couponing, and free goods), marketing, new product introductions, entry into our distribution networks, and other competitive behavior by other suppliers and by wholesalers and traditional and e-commerce retailers, could adversely affect our growth, business, and financial results. While we seek to take advantage of the efficiencies and opportunities that large retail customers can offer, they often seek lower pricing and increased purchase volume flexibility, offer competing private label products, and represent a large number of other competing products. If the buying power of these large retail customers continues to increase, it could negatively affect our financial results. Further, while we believe we have sufficient scale to succeed relative to our major competitors, we nevertheless face a risk that continuing consolidation of large beverage alcohol companies could put us at a competitive disadvantage.

Consolidation, whether domestically or internationally, among spirits producers, distributors, wholesalers, suppliers, or retailers and the increased growth of the e-commerce environment across the consumer product goods market have created and could continue to create a more challenging competitive landscape for our products. Consolidation at any level could hinder the distribution and sale of our products as a result of reduced attention and resources allocated to our brands because our brands might represent a smaller portion of the new business portfolio. Furthermore, consolidation of distributors may lead to the erosion of margins. Changes in distributors' strategies, including a reduction in the number of brands they carry, the allocation of shelf space for our competitors' brands, or private label products, may adversely affect our growth, business, financial results, and market share. Our competitors may respond to industry and economic conditions and shifts in consumer behaviors more rapidly or effectively than we do. To remain competitive, we must be agile and efficient in adopting digital technologies and building analytical capabilities, which our competitors may be able to achieve with more agility and resources.

paragraphs: Brown-Forman Corporation (the "Company," "Brown-Forman," "we," "us," or "our" below) 於 1933 年根據德拉瓦州法律設立，為 1870 年創立的合夥企業之繼承者，後於 1901 年根據肯塔基州法律設立。我們主要製造、蒸餾、灌裝、進口、出口、行銷及銷售多種飲料酒精產品，並使用知名品牌。我們在全球六大洲僱用約 4,900 名員工（不計兼職或臨時工作者），包括美國約 1,900 名員工（約 7% 為工會會員）及 700 名員工於美國肯塔基州路易斯維爾，為本公司世界總部所在地。根據國際葡萄酒與烈酒研究（IWSR），我們為美國所有權的 premium-plus 烈酒公司中規模最大者。我們根據紐約證券交易所規則為一 "受控公司"，因布朗家族持有本公司逾 50% 的投票權股票。
有關近期發展之討論，請參閱 "項目 7. 管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之分析 – 管理層摘要。"

自 1870 年以 Old Forester Kentucky Straight Bourbon Whisky – 我們的創立品牌 – 開始，歷經各世代，我們已建立包含超過 40 種烈酒及即飲（RTD）雞尾酒品牌的產品組合，其中包括本行業中一些最知名且最受歡迎的商標。我們產品組閤中最重要的標誌性品牌為 Jack Daniel's Tennessee Whiskey，為全球銷售第一的美國威士忌。1 在 Jack Daniel's 產品組閤中，Jack Daniel's 14-Year-Old Tennessee Whiskey 獲得世界最佳 Tennessee Whiskey 獎項，而 Jack Daniel's Bonded 則獲頒最佳 Tennessee Whiskey（無年份標示）獎項，於 2026 年世界威士忌大獎中。我們的高階波本威士忌 Old Forester，在 2026 年舊金山烈酒大賽中獲得了認可，其中 Old Forester 1870 Original Batch 及 Old Forester 1897 Bottled in Bond 都獲得了雙金（最高榮譽）。

headings: 與我們業務及營運相關的風險
我們的業務表現大幅取決於 Jack Daniel's 品牌家族的持續健康狀況。
我們的通路至消費者模式變更，以及飲料酒類製造商、經銷商、批發商、供應商及零售商之間的合併，可能會妨礙我們產品的行銷、銷售或分銷。
我們面臨來自美國及外國政府貿易政策、關稅及進出口規範變更的風險。
生產設施中斷可能會對我們的業務造成不利影響。
供需預測的內在不確定性可能會對我們的業務造成不利影響，特別是在我們的陳年產品方面。
水、原材料、產品原料或勞動力的成本提高或無法取得，可能會對我們的財務結果造成不利影響。
不利的經濟條件可能會對我們的營運及結果造成負面影響。
我們可能無法成功執行投資、收購、處置及其他戰略交易的策略。
負面宣傳或我們無法認知、回應並有效管理社交媒體影響力增加的情況，可能影響我們的營運表現。
產品回收或其他產品責任聲索可能對我們的銷售造成重大且不利的影響。
我們若無法吸引或留住關鍵人才，可能對我們的業務造成不利影響。
我們的業務面臨與健康疫情及大流行相關的風險，可能對我們的業務、營運、現金流及財務結果造成重大且不利的影響。
與我們全球營運相關的風險
我們的全球業務面臨商業、政治及財務風險。
未能遵守反貪污法律、貿易制裁及限制，或其他類似法律或法規，可能對我們的業務及財務結果造成重大不利影響。
外幣交換率相對於美元的波動，可能對我們的財務結果產生重大不利影響。
本公司信用評級遭降級或潛在降級，可能不利於我們的借款成本與取得信貸及資本市場的機會，進而對我們的財務狀況產生負面影響。
法律與法規風險
國家及地方政府可能制定規範或進行調查，可能限制我們的業務活動或增加我們的成本。
稅收增加或稅務規則的變更，可能對我們的財務結果產生不利影響。
我們行銷與銷售產品的能力，高度依賴社會對飲酒的態度與政府政策，而這些政策源自並影響該態度。
針對我們產品的重大額外標籤、警告要求或產品可取得性的限制，可能抑制受影響產品的銷售。
仿冒或對我們智慧財產權權利保護不足，可能對我們的業務前景產生不利影響。
訴訟及法律爭議可能使本公司面臨財務及聲譽風險。
與網路安全及資料隱私權相關的風險
與本公司股權結構及企業治理架構相關的風險
布朗家族擁有控制股東會批准事項結果的能力。
paragraphs: 我們相信以下討論識別出可能對我們業務產生重大影響的風險與不確定性。如果任何上述風險實際發生，將可能對我們的業務、營運結果、現金流或財務狀況造成重大且不利的影響。此外，尚有其他風險目前尚未為我們所知，或目前認為不重要，也可能對我們的業務、營運結果、現金流或財務狀況造成重大且不利的影響。

Jack Daniel's 品牌家族為我們的營業收入主要驅動力，Jack Daniel's 是一個具有忠實消費者羣的國際知名商標。我們投入大量努力與資源來保護與維護該品牌的真實性、工藝與品質聲譽。品牌的聲譽價值在很大程度上取決於消費者觀感，即使單一事件造成損害，特別是引起廣泛負面宣傳的情況，也可能對這些觀感產生不利影響，並削弱消費者對品牌的信任與信心。Jack Daniel's 品牌家族的聲譽價值受到重大損害，將對我們的業務造成不利影響。考慮到 Jack Daniel's 對我們整體成功的重要性，若因負面宣傳或其他原因導致我們 Jack Daniel's 產品銷售出現重大或持續下滑，將對我們的財務結果產生負面影響。此外，若我們未能成功維持或提升 Jack Daniel's 品牌對現有及未來消費者的相關性，將可能影響我們的業務與營運結果。

我們使用多種商業模式在世界各地不同國家市場推廣與銷售產品。在美國，我們將產品銷售給經銷商，由經銷商再銷售至零售通路或電商零售商，或在控制酒精銷售的州，銷售給州政府，再由州政府銷售給零售客戶與消費者。在非美國市場，我們使用多種通路至消費者模式，且在許多市場，我們依賴第三方進行產品的銷售、行銷與分銷。我們擁有並運營17家分銷公司，分佈於18個國家。從第三方分銷模式轉為自有分銷模式是一項重大工程，並使我們面臨每個受影響地理區域的額外營運與執行風險。若我們未能成功執行通路至消費者策略，包括任何轉為自有分銷的過程，將可能影響產品的銷售與行銷。
任何我們通路至消費者模式或重要市場的經銷商發生變動，可能導致短期或長期的銷售中斷、成本增加，並影響我們與該經銷商的其他商業關係。我們分銷網路的中斷或經銷商、經銷商或零售商的產品存貨水準波動，可能對特定期間的營運結果產生負面影響。此外，其他供應商以及我們品牌的經銷商與零售商所提供的產品，會直接與我們的產品競爭商品展示空間、促銷展示與消費者購買。

價格（包括價格促銷、折扣、優惠券與免費商品）、行銷、新產品推出、進入我們的分銷網路，以及其他供應商與經銷商與傳統及電商零售商的競爭行為，可能對我們的成長、業務與財務結果產生不利影響。雖然我們致力於利用大型零售客戶所提供的效率與機會，但這些客戶往往要求更低的價格與更高的採購彈性，提供競爭的自有品牌產品，並代表大量其他競爭產品。若這些大型零售客戶的購買力持續增加，可能對我們的財務結果產生負面影響。此外，雖然我們認為我們的規模足以相較於主要競爭對手取得成功，但我們仍面臨持續合併大型酒類公司可能使我們處於競爭劣勢的風險。

無論國內或國際，酒類製造商、經銷商、經銷商、供應商或零售商的合併，以及消費性產品市場電商環境的成長，已創造並可能持續創造更嚴峻的競爭環境。任何層級的合併都可能因資源與關注度分配減少，使我們的品牌在新業務組閤中佔比較小，而影響我們產品的分銷與銷售。此外，經銷商的合併可能導致邊際利潤的減少。經銷商策略的變動，包括減少所銷售的品牌數量、分配給競爭品牌或自有品牌商品的展示空間，可能對我們的成長、業務、財務結果與市佔率產生不利影響。我們的競爭對手可能比我們更快或更有效地應對產業與經濟條件的變化以及消費者行為的轉變。為維持競爭力，我們必須靈活且高效地採用數位科技與建立分析能力，而我們的競爭對手可能擁有更靈活與資源的優勢。
